items.q: Strongest single predictor of future suicide death is what?
items.exp: Prior attempt (especially recent or high lethality) outweighs demographic factors in predicting death, though most attempters still do not die, showing prediction limits requiring formulation based care.
r: Incorrect. Sex stratifies but weaker than attempt history.
Correct. Previous attempt predicts strongest.
Incorrect. Unemployment contributes modestly.
Incorrect. Family history raises risk less than own attempt.

items.q: Asking a depressed patient directly about suicidal thoughts does what to risk?
o: Plants the idea and raises risk
Does not increase risk and is essential assessment
items.exp: Evidence and guidelines confirm direct enquiry does not induce suicide and uncovers treatable intent; avoidance misses plans and means needing intervention.
r: Incorrect. Myth contradicted by evidence.
Correct. Ask directly; it does not implant.
Incorrect. No such legal bar exists.
Incorrect. Assessment belongs at presentation, not after.

items.q: Which drug has specific anti suicidal evidence in bipolar disorder?
items.exp: Lithium reduces suicide and all cause mortality in bipolar disorder beyond mood stabilisation in meta analyses, influencing drug choice in high risk patients with adherence and monitoring capacity.
r: Incorrect. Carbamazepine lacks this evidence.
Correct. Lithium anti suicidal effect.
Incorrect. Valproate evidence is weaker and inconsistent.
Incorrect. Lamotrigine prevents depression relapse without proven suicide reduction.

items.q: In schizophrenia, which antipsychotic is licensed to reduce recurrent suicidal behaviour?
items.exp: Clozapine reduced suicidal behaviour in the InterSePT trial population with schizophrenia at high risk, an indication beyond treatment resistance, with its monitoring burden accepted for this benefit.
r: Incorrect. Haloperidol has no such indication.
Correct. Clozapine anti suicidal indication in schizophrenia.
Incorrect. Aripiprazole lacks this trial evidence.
Incorrect. Olanzapine was comparator, not winner.
items.kp: Clozapine also shields against suicide in schizophrenia.

items.q: Highest risk interval after psychiatric inpatient discharge is what?
items.exp: Suicide rates spike in first week and month post discharge (transition, illness persisting, support gap), mandating follow up within days, crisis contacts and means safety before leave.
r: Correct. Days to weeks after discharge peak.
Incorrect. Year later risk is lower.
Incorrect. Discharge does not normalise risk instantly.
Incorrect. Anniversaries are minor beside transitions.
items.kp: The week home is the danger week.

items.q: A collaborative safety plan differs from a no suicide contract how?
o: Safety plan lists warning signs, coping steps, contacts and means restriction; contracts are ineffective and not recommended
items.exp: Stanley and Brown safety planning is an evidence based prioritised coping list made with the patient; no harm contracts lack evidence, may falsely reassure clinicians and are discouraged.
r: Incorrect. Contracts guarantee nothing.
Correct. Concrete safety plan, not contract.
Incorrect. They differ fundamentally in evidence.
Incorrect. Safety planning is voluntary collaboration.

items.q: Means restriction reduces suicide because of which principle?
o: Suicidal crises are often brief and method substitution is incomplete
items.exp: Many attempts are impulsive during short crises; blocking lethal means (barriers, pack sizes, firearm storage) lets crises pass and substitution to equally lethal methods is incomplete, lowering population deaths.
r: Correct. Brief crises plus incomplete substitution saves lives.
Incorrect. It is environmental, not antidepressant.
Incorrect. Ideation may persist while deaths fall.
Incorrect. It is compassionate engineering, not punishment.
items.kp: Put time and distance between urge and lethal means.

items.q: After deliberate self poisoning, guideline care before discharge includes what?
o: Psychosocial assessment by trained staff for every presentation
items.exp: Every self-harm presentation warrants biopsychosocial assessment (intent, mental state, needs, risk formulation) before discharge regardless of medical clearance or repetition status, per NICE pattern guidance.
r: Incorrect. Medical fitness alone misses psychiatric need.
Correct. Psychosocial assessment for all.
Incorrect. Police role is not clinical assessment substitute.
Incorrect. First presentations also predict future risk.
items.kp: Medically clear is not assessment done.

items.q: Which presentation pattern most raises concern for imminent risk in interview?
o: Passive wish to be dead, strong family support, no plans
Detailed plan, means acquired, farewell acts, hopelessness and intoxication
Chronic thoughts for years with coping plan
items.exp: Specific planning, acquired means, preparatory or farewell behaviour, hopelessness and disinhibiting intoxication together formulate high imminent risk needing urgent intervention, though no checklist replaces judgement.
r: Incorrect. Lower concern pattern with protection.
Correct. Plan plus means plus preparation plus hopelessness.
Incorrect. Chronic managed ideation differs in imminence.
Incorrect. Transient regretted thought is lower acuity.
items.kp: Plan, means and goodbyes together alarm most.

items.q: Repetition of self-harm after an index episode occurs in roughly what proportion within a year, guiding follow up intensity?
o: About 15 to 20 percent, with suicide risk many fold population rate
items.exp: Roughly one in six repeat within a year and suicide risk after self-harm is tens of times general population, justifying assertive follow up, therapy (DBT, CBT based) and safety planning for all.
r: Incorrect. Far higher than one percent.
Correct. Fifteen to twenty percent repeat.
Incorrect. Most do not repeat in a year.
Incorrect. Extensively studied epidemiology.
items.kp: One in six repeat; follow them closely.
